metadata.title: 72 Comments, One Plan
metadata.audience: Students and practitioners learning to use and report on AI systems
metadata.fellow: Janvi Chitroda, AI Data Engineer volunteer, Medhavy project, Humanitarians AI
metadata.source: inbox/term2-week10/term2-week10-video-content.md (Week 10); narration supplied verbatim and pre-approved by Janvi (2026-10-28)
metadata.note: Project update. Thesis: Professor Gultepe's second review (6 big-picture points, 72 comments) was applied systematically — comments extracted and sorted into four types, six batched CRITIQ prompts under one set of hard rules, every article count traced to its origin (71,000 had no data source: derived by subtraction, shown on screen only as unsourced/derived and put on the do-not-use list), repository facts from the code, batches 1–3 run and two CRITIQ-introduced errors caught. The revision work is Janvi's. Only Professor Brown and Professor Gultepe may be named. Every on-screen number appears in the Week 10 source as written.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude composer, ask lands answered. Required intro line + AI-narration disclosure.
beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Janvi and this video is about working through a 72-comment review of our paper without losing anything. This narration is an AI-generated voice; the work is mine.

props.command: My paper's review has 72 comments across every section. How do I apply them without losing anything?
output: Extract every comment with its anchor text
Sort them by what each one needs
Apply them in batches with shared rules

beats.role_note: Review card: '6 big-picture points' + '72 comments' fanning across every section; 'one pass risks lost content and broken numbers'.
beats.narration_text: Professor Gultepe sent her second review: six big-picture points and 72 comments across every section. Applying all of that in one pass would risk lost content and broken numbers.
beats.visual_intent: Review card: '6 big-picture points' + '72 comments' fanning across every section; 'one pass risks lost content and broken numbers'.

show.event: one pass: lost content, broken numbers

beats.role_note: Script card extracts 72 comments (anchor text + section) → four bins: paper-only edits · facts to check in the repository · figure work · tables to build.
beats.narration_text: So I wrote a script to extract all 72 comments with their anchor text and section, and sorted them into four types: paper-only edits, facts to check in the repository, figure work, and tables to build.
beats.visual_intent: Script card extracts 72 comments (anchor text + section) → four bins: paper-only edits · facts to check in the repository · figure work · tables to build.

beats.role_note: Six batch cards under one shared-rules card: no number change without a source · no invented facts · no em dashes · keep every comment · report OLD → NEW.
beats.narration_text: Then I designed six batched CRITIQ prompts with one shared set of rules: no number changes without a source, no invented facts, no em dashes, keep every comment, and report the old text and new text for every change.
beats.visual_intent: Six batch cards under one shared-rules card: no number change without a source · no invented facts · no em dashes · keep every comment · report OLD → NEW.

beats.role_note: Number trace table: ~81,000 → substring matches · 10,055 → exact matches · 10,049 → after 6 duplicates removed; each with a source tick. 71,000 shown only as 'no source'.
beats.narration_text: One comment questioned the step from 71,000 articles to 10,000. So I traced every count to its origin. About 81,000 came from substring matching. 10,055 were exact matches, and 10,049 remained after six duplicates were removed.
beats.visual_intent: Number trace table: ~81,000 → substring matches · 10,055 → exact matches · 10,049 → after 6 duplicates removed; each with a source tick. 71,000 shown only as 'no source'.

beats.role_note: Row '71,000 · only in the manuscript' with stamp 'no data source'; 'derived: ~81,000 minus ~10,000'; status 'Verified' struck → 'Unsourced'; 'do not use' list card.
beats.narration_text: But 71,000 appeared only in the manuscript. It had been worked out by subtraction and written in as if it were measured, and it had been marked verified by mistake. I added it to a do-not-use list on my master number sheet.
beats.visual_intent: Row '71,000 · only in the manuscript' with stamp 'no data source'; 'derived: ~81,000 minus ~10,000'; status 'Verified' struck → 'Unsourced'; 'do not use' list card.

show.event: 71,000 · only in the manuscript · no data source

beats.role_note: Repository fact cards: artifact checker = rule-based, up to 2 retries · generation model = GPT-4o-mini · GO gate: 3 categories set, 2 reachable.
beats.narration_text: Some comments needed answers only the code could give. The artifact checker is rule-based, with up to two retries. The generation model is G P T four o mini. And the Gene Ontology gate is set for three categories, but only two are reachable in production.
beats.visual_intent: Repository fact cards: artifact checker = rule-based, up to 2 retries · generation model = GPT-4o-mini · GO gate: 3 categories set, 2 reachable.

show.event: answers only the code could give
artifact checker: rule-based, up to 2 retries

beats.role_note: Batch cards 1 terminology · 2 structure · 3 line-level fixes; chip '2 errors CRITIQ introduced: caught'. (Split from Janvi's B07 so the handoff stays a pure composer beat; narration verbatim.)
beats.narration_text: I ran the first three batches: terminology, structure, and line-level fixes. And I checked CRITIQ's output. It had introduced two errors, which I caught and fixed.
beats.visual_intent: Batch cards 1 terminology · 2 structure · 3 line-level fixes; chip '2 errors CRITIQ introduced: caught'. (Split from Janvi's B07 so the handoff stays a pure composer beat; narration verbatim.)
